title: November 4 — NeuronBeach: soma pool, AIS wave machine and learned replay
summary: A browser-based neuron-as-coast visualization and a six-unit sequence-learning model translate the wave-written beach metaphor into dendritic low-pass propagation, AIS spike initiation, back-propagating timing plasticity and reward gating. Source-reported controls show 30/30 held-out six-neuron sequence replays versus 0/30 for shuffled or non-learning controls, with notable eight-neuron and homeostasis failures. Synaptic sandbars are numerical weights updated by scripted rules, not physical sediment dynamics.

nodes.claim: Two dependency-free HTML/JavaScript simulators illustrate one neuron as a coast and connect six neurons into an all-to-all delayed network with a low-pass dendritic graph, thresholded AIS, backpropagation, eligibility traces, spike-timing plasticity, inhibition and an optional reward/tide gate.
nodes.survived: Single-cell controls demonstrate summation, filtered fast ripples, a tuft-plus-backwash burst window and synaptic potentiation. Network held-out tests on seeds 101–130 report full ordered replay 30/30 after 15 lessons, 0/30 after shuffled order, no training, frozen weights or missing tide; only 14/30 without inhibition. Weak pings leave lasting weights unchanged but do alter a transient eligibility trace.
nodes.killed: This is not physical erosion: synaptic sandbars are numerical weights changed by programmed rules; axonal propagation and Ca plateau are simplified switches rather than biophysical channel models. Eight neurons at fixed sand budget replay only 7/30 (tide 0/30); homeostasis in the six-neuron dev ring fails (0/10). It has not shown context-dependent recall, multiple memories, real units or improved learning beyond known STDP and inhibition.
nodes.era: November 4: a neuron made legible as a coast

edges.why: NeuronBeach explicitly credits the ComputingBeachClaude beach metaphor. It reuses the conceptual wave/medium picture, but replaces stress-driven physical sand modification with programmed synaptic weights and neuron-like switches, rather than a direct solver fork.
Both work on neuronal signal propagation, compartmental AIS/gating and learned response geometry. This is a cross-project conceptual parallel, not documented code inheritance.

motifs.title: A wave crosses a pathway; a spike can change how the next wave crosses
motifs.description: The neuron-coast visual makes dendritic filtering, thresholded regeneration, back-propagating timing coincidence and reward-gated traces observable in one learning loop. The demonstration is a scripted STDP and inhibition model rather than self-eroding sediment. A weak read can alter transient eligibility without changing persistent weight.
